title: Admin gap runbook: SSO mapping reconciliation and controlled failover for RBAC v2 migration
creator: Aisha Khan
description: Create an operator-focused runbook and automation suite to detect and repair admin-permission divergence during RBAC v1 -> v2 migration. The scope covers SSO/SAML attribute reconciliation, dual-write convergence checks, audit duplication for immutable streams, controlled failover triggers, and customer-facing rollback/opt-in procedures.
acceptance_criteria: Parity: Admin-role parity >= 99.99% for top 100 orgs (by seat count) after backfill sweep
Convergence: Dual-write lag monitoring shows <5s median and <60s 95th percentile during canary rollout
Audit: Every authorization decision during migration is duplicated to immutable audit stream (s3://redwood-audit-immutable/rbacv2/) for 30 days
Rollback: Automated rollback path successfully reverts role assignments and SSO mappings in under 15 minutes in staging dry-runs
Customer comms: Customer opt-in portal and templated notice posted to support portal with clear remediation steps
tasks: Implement reconciliation worker that consumes SAML attribute deltas and emits reconciliation patches (GitHub PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rbac/PR-3421)
Add dual-write monitoring dashboard (Grafana) with custom alert rules and sampling policy
Wire audit duplication to immutable stream and add SHA256 checksums to each record
Build canary orchestration script that selects customers based on risk score and seat distribution
Author customer-facing rollback/opt-in templates and post to support knowledge base
runbook_steps: 1) PRE-CHECK: Run parity report for target org (script: infra/tools/rbac/parity_check.py) and capture baseline
2) ENABLE DUAL-WRITE: Turn on dual-write for target shard (toggle: feature/dual_write_admins). Verify writes land in both v1/v2 stores
3) START RECONCILER: Deploy reconciliation worker in staging with dry-run=true. Observe emitted patches in /tmp/recon-sample.json
4) APPLY BACKFILL: Run backfill job with rate limit 200 ops/min. Monitor metrics: admin_parity, backfill_rate, error_rate
5) MONITOR AUDIT DUP: Verify each auth event appears in immutable stream and that checksums match (script: tools/audit/verify_stream.sh)
6) CANARY CUTOVER: Promote 5 low-risk customers via orchestration script. Maintain 24h watch with SLO guardrails. If parity delta >0.01% for any canary, trigger rollback
7) FAILOVER: If automated rollback triggers, execute failover playbook to re-enable v1 authoritative store, pause writes to v2, and create incident Slack channel #sec-rbac-cutover
8) CUSTOMER NOTIFY: Use templated email and support ticket macro to notify affected customers of action and next steps
9) POST-VALIDATION: After 72h stable, schedule wide rollout in waves of increasing risk profile
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Missing SAML attributes cause admin-loss for some users. Mitigation: Conservative canary selection, attribute presence checks, and prefill missing attributes with admin-holdover mapping
Risk: Reconciler introduces bad writes. Mitigation: Dry-run mode, op-logging, and reversible patch format with tombstone markers
Risk: Audit stream lag/duplication gaps. Mitigation: End-to-end checksum validation and fallback to buffered upload on failure
Risk: Customer panic from unexpected permission changes. Mitigation: Proactive comms, opt-in gating, and dedicated support SLA during rollout
stakeholders: Design: Priya Nair (for support portal templates)
testing_and_dry_runs: Staging dry-run executed 2025-02-20: reconciler emitted 3,412 patch candidates, 0.03% flagged for manual review
Chaos test 2025-02-25: Simulated SSO attribute drop; automated fallback mapping preserved admin access for 98.7% of synthetic users
Rollback rehearsal 2025-03-01: Completed in 9 minutes in staging with no data loss
open_questions: Should the reconciler auto-apply small fixes (<3% diff) or always require PM approval?
Do we allow customers to opt-out permanently, or only for the duration of the migration window?
What is the SLA for support response when a customer reports a missing admin after rollouts?
